bio_en: Hrach Papazian came from a wealthy family of Yozgat and was sent young to Constantinople, where he threw himself into revolutionary work. From Constantinople to Berlin and Rome and back again, he became an embodiment of the 'Armenian Nemesis' that punished those responsible for the Genocide, though he never wrote down his memoirs. Over forty years of revolutionary and public work he became one of the ARF's responsible leaders. He died in Beirut in August 1960, and his funeral on 18 August was led by Catholicos Zareh I.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. The specific Nemesis operations he took part in are not named in the texts read.
